claim: VIF confidence calibration benchmarks show ECE ≤0.05 (well-calibrated confidence).
Confidence bands (A/B/C) match actual outcomes: Band A (0.95-1.00) matches 95%+ accuracy.
κ-gating benchmarks show 95%+ effectiveness in blocking low-confidence operations.
Calibration drift detection validates continuous monitoring prevents calibration degradation.
Bayesian calibration validation proves Bayesian updates improve confidence accuracy over time.
Confidence tracking benchmarks show 90%+ of confidence scores match actual outcomes.
ECE measures how well AI confidence matches actual accuracy. Formula: ECE = Σ|conf - acc|/N. Target: ECE ≤0.05.
AIM-OS distinguishes four confidence types: Direction, Execution, Autonomous, and Collaborative to prevent inflation.
Calibration model tracks bias per task category (documentation, code, organizational) to adjust raw confidence.
Expected Calibration Error (ECE) measures how well-calibrated probabilistic predictions are.
VIF performance characteristics: ECE calculation ~10ms per 1,000 predictions, κ-gate evaluation <2ms per operation, witness creation ~10ms overhead, calibration updates asynchronous.
VIF performance metrics: Witness creation latency target <10ms, confidence extraction latency target <5ms, κ-gate latency target <2ms, ECE calculation latency target <10ms per 1,000 predictions.
VIF calibration loop: Track outcome → Calculate ECE → Assess quality (ECE ≤0.05) → Alert if poor (ECE >0.10) → Update model to improve calibration.
VIF performance improvements: Witness optimization (5ms → 1ms, 80% improvement), batch operations (5x speedup), storage optimization (50% reduction), calibration management (ECE <0.05).

VIF troubleshooting for calibration: Over-confidence (retrain with failure data), under-confidence (retrain with success data), calibration drift (investigate data drift), bias (apply mitigation techniques).
VIF operational best practices for confidence calibration include continuous monitoring, automated retraining, feedback integration, bias audits, and version control.
